info.name: Work Order Portal API
info.description:
Auto-generated Postman collection for the Work Order Portal (NestJS) API.

## Getting started
1. Set the `base_url` variable (default `http://localhost:3000`).
2. Run **Auth → Login** (or **Register company + owner**). A test script stores the JWT in the `{{token}}` collection variable.
3. All other requests inherit Bearer auth from the collection using `{{token}}` — no manual copying needed.

## Automation
Many list/create requests include test scripts that capture resource IDs (`companyId`, `serviceId`, `formId`, `workOrderId`, etc.) into collection variables, so downstream requests can be run in sequence with the Collection Runner.

item.name: Auth

request.description: Step 1 of 2. Validates and emails a 6-digit OTP; the account is NOT created yet. role must be one of: client, unassigned_staff. Complete with "Verify OTP".
Step 1 of 2. Emails a 6-digit OTP; the company/owner is created only after "Verify OTP". In dev mode (no SMTP configured) the OTP is printed to the server console.

Step 2 of 2. Verifies the emailed OTP and creates the account. For company signups the response includes a token, saved to {{token}} automatically. Set the {{otp}} variable to the code from the email/console first.

exec: const json = (() => { try { return pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { return null; } })();
if (json && json.data) {
const raw = json.data.token || json.data.accessToken || '';
const jwt = String(raw).replace(/^Bearer\s+/i, '');
if (jwt) {
pm.collectionVariables.set('token', jwt);
console.log('Auth token saved to {{token}}');
const companyId = (json.data.user && json.data.user.company && json.data.user.company._id) || (json.data.company && json.data.company._id);
if (companyId) pm.collectionVariables.set('companyId', companyId);
pm.test('Status is 2xx', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.below(300));

item.description: Authentication flow. Registration is two-step: "Register" (step 1) emails a 6-digit OTP, then "Verify OTP" (step 2) creates the account. In dev mode (no SMTP) the OTP is printed to the server console. "Login" and "Verify OTP" store the JWT in {{token}} for every other request.
